A few more pictures of this stunning clone. These were taken around late December 2022:



A slightly nicer shot on the Canon. These winter colors are just unreal.


Here's what it looks like right now. The early season pitchers are definitely more spindly as per the alabamensis parentage. I'm very excited to breed with this plant, as the floppy lid of Hummer's Hammerhead has dominated in crosses before (for example S. 'Chris') and Monks Head Hammerhead has even more exaggerated lids than HH. Ideally, future work will yield plants with strong full-season growth while keeping those ridiculous lids. What would you like to see this crossed with?

posts.body_html:
Hear ye, hear ye! MHH fall pitchers have arrived! This is definitely the time of year when this plant really comes into its own. The biggest lid so far is just over 3” wide and 2.5” long, sitting atop a pitcher less than 9” tall (By the way, I have some breeding projects in the pipeline to hopefully shorten the pitchers and exaggerate that ratio even further, but that’s at least a few years out…) It won’t be long until this plant looks like a clump of red and yellow mushrooms once again. Can’t wait!



That lid angle is just stoooopid!! Check out all the white in the tube, btw! Super “stretchy” in both the front and back—you don’t often get that with leucophylla/moorei plants which skew towards a much whiter back than front. Psittacina crosses can do some weird stuff…


Here’s another shot of developing fenestrations—see how they stretch way down and then abruptly stop? Rob Co has made some hammerhead crosses that amplify this “white sock” super well. Very cool genetics in there!


First encounters… of the hammerhead kind!

posts.body_html: I've long complained that MHH is a slouch in the spring, only coming into its own with its magnificent fall crop. However, this year I'm totally eating my words! Despite pushing up NINE flowers (and this was its first year flowering...), my clump still had the energy for some absolutely marvelous spring pitchers with massive lids. The one pictured was the most photogenic--I seriously cannot wait to see how the offspring of this beauty turn out...
